text:
Pavel Dorofeyev came to the Rangers from Vegas as a finisher, and the chances have followed him: 57 shots and 8.3 expected goals in 19 games, the most dangerous individual looks on the team by rate. The goals have lagged. He has 6, on a 10.5% shooting rate against a talent range closer to 14%.

The bigger number is around him. New York has scored about 20 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Dorofeyev on the ice. That is an enormous gap for 19 games, and it explains why an even-strength line winning 54% of expected goals has so little to show for it. He has been heating up lately, with goals in three of his last five games.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him on the end of the best passes last season, and Evolving-Hockey liked his defense more than people expect from a sniper. Our range has him around 30 goals by April. We'd be surprised if he isn't scoring at a much higher clip by Christmas.
headline: Dorofeyev is getting chances, not results
